about: Server-only, 48 holders (every Anubis-driven entity). The component is an ls::anubis::savegame::Writer moved into the ECS (macOS: EntityCommandBuffer::AddComponentUnchecked<StateComponent, Writer>(Writer&&); ls::anubis::System::Save fills the Writer; ls::anubis::savegame::Reader::Reader(Writer&&) consumes it). It holds the serialized Anubis behaviour state: a constant pointer, seven containers (a 0x70-byte block moved by bg3.exe+0x38284F0) and one more array. Not itself a savegame model (savemodel.py matched only unrelated StateComponents).

evidence.says: The component is a Writer (macOS AddComponentUnchecked<StateComponent, Writer>); ls::anubis::savegame::Writer::Writer(Registry&) (AnubisFramework.dll+0x105AF0) stores '*(Registry**)this = param_1' before constructing the Header at +8; macOS Reader::Reader(Writer&&) (bg3_macos_x64+0x6740F00) copies Writer +0 to Reader +0 first.

Writer +8 is model::Header; this is Header +0. AnubisFramework.dll+0x1196D0 ls::anubis::savegame::model::Header::Visit visits the Header's seven arrays in order with keys built from string literals: +0 'Scalar' (DAT_1801b0e38, init AnubisFramework.dll+0x15E50), +0x10 'Table' (+0x16090), +0x20 'TableEntry' (+0x160C0), +0x30 'Variable', +0x40 tree key, +0x50 'Operation', +0x60 'Component' - the last four match the arrays already named Variables / Trees / Operations / Components from macOS Header::~Header (bg3_macos_x64+0x667E5F0).

Header +0x30 = DynamicArray<ls::anubis::savegame::model::Variable> (macOS ~Header); Windows destructor bg3.exe+0x3828670 resizes it with bg3.exe+0x3839060 (0x20-byte elements: STDString + qword). Live heap, capacity 0x1F..0x80.

Header +0x40 = PagedArray<ls::anubis::savegame::model::Tree, AnubisPagedArrayOps> (macOS ~Header: RemoveAll, then frees each page and the page table, clears the u16 page count at +0x4A); Windows bg3.exe+0x3839240 destroys pages of 0x28-byte elements holding a string and a FixedString. Page table pointer.
page-size shift of the paged array (Windows move helper bg3.exe+0x38284F0); live 9.
page count (macOS ~Header loops to and clears the u16 at Header+0x4A = component +0x52); live 1.
element count of the paged array; live 1.
Header +0x50 = DynamicArray<ls::anubis::savegame::model::Operation> (macOS ~Header); Windows resizes it with the same 0x20-byte element function bg3.exe+0x3839060. Live empty.
Header +0x60 = DynamicArray<ls::anubis::savegame::model::Component> (macOS ~Header); Windows bg3.exe+0x3839460 walks 0x40-byte elements with destructor bg3.exe+0x383CEC0. Live capacity 1 size 1.

Writer +0x78 = DynamicArray<ls::anubis::savegame::model::TypeArray> (macOS ~Writer reallocates it to 0 and frees it); Windows component destructor bg3.exe+0x3850240 calls bg3.exe+0x3839730(comp+0x78, 0) (0x20-byte elements, destructor bg3.exe+0x383D230). Live capacity 0x29 size 0x29.

open_questions: Element sizes of the three plain arrays at +8, +0x18, +0x28 (Header +0..+0x20) are not established.
Meaning of the qword at +0x18 of Variable/Operation elements, of +0/+8/+0x38 of Component elements, and the nested 0x40-byte value elements.
The pointer at +0; member names (only the macOS type names of the containers are known).
Coverage.h's AnubisSavegameReader (ls::anubis::savegame::LoadingComponent) has the same first 0x88 bytes; it could reuse these names.
